atoms.text: Fingal's cave is one of the most special in Scotland. Its hexagonal basalt columns make it look like it has been built by humans, but it was formed naturally during the tertiary period.

atoms.b: Have you heard of Fingal's Cave? That thing also looks quite spooky.
Legend says that this interestingly formed cave was home to a giant called Benandonner. It is located in the Isle of Staffa near the west coast of Scotland.
I thought it was Fingal's cave?

That's what it is called today. Fingal is a hero of Celtic mythology and Benandonner's opponent. Fingal was based on the other side of the sea in Ireland. The two insulted each other over miles across the water. As a consequence, Benandonnor came over the Giant's Causeway, a water bridge to Ireland, to fight Fingal.

The two insulted each other over miles across the water. As a consequence, Benandonnor came over the Giant's Causeway, a water bridge to Ireland, to fight Fingal.

atoms.b: And who won according to the legend?

Well, actually no one. Since Fingal knew he couldn't beat the giant, he decided to trick him. When Benandonnor came, Fingal was wrapped in a cloth like a baby. His wife told the giant that Fingal was currently hunting, and she was alone with their newborn. Of course, Benandonnor got afraid of who might be the father of this huge baby and quickly took off.
